newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds rose for the second successive day to end the week on a firmer note, ralling in tandem with German Bunds after weak U.S. production data.
But volumes remained at low levels, a situation attributed by market players to the current low level of guilder interest rates, which are frightening potential buyers.
U.S. data showed a fall in industrial output in October when a rise had been forecast. "People went short on those figures," said a trader, adding the market rose as they covered positions.
He said there was no liquidity, while another trader said the U.S. data was the only point of interest today.

Ten-year government bond yields, at 5.74 pct, are at the lowest level since February 1994 and, according to four of five banks polled by Reuters, are forecast to rise to 5.80-5.85 percent in the next month.
But a dealer said he expected German bonds, and hence their Dutch equivalents, to resume their rise toward the end of the year because of cash inflows to institutional investors.
"Institutional investors still need to invest that money," he said.
